subject.title: feat(linux): native gateway transport for Quick Chat — device identity, TLS pinning, ack-driven sends

question: Should the Linux desktop app receive the same silent direct-local pairing and privileged native-UI admission class as macOS, iOS, and Android once the compatibility omissions are fixed?
rationale: The change is a deliberate expansion of Gateway device trust and pairing behavior; code review can confirm mechanics but cannot choose the permanent product security boundary.

options.title: Approve the scoped native trust class
options.body: Accept Linux as a first-class native UI client after the alias, trusted-proxy handoff, and changelog corrections land.

options.title: Retain the existing transport boundary
options.body: Do not grant Linux silent native-device pairing until maintainers choose a narrower enrollment or approval model.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped native trust class
recommendation.body: Accept Linux as a first-class native UI client after the alias, trusted-proxy handoff, and changelog corrections land.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the existing Linux Quick Chat surface and authored the proposed Gateway-device integration.
